product_intent: Aegis should act like a sensible, context-aware overseer that helps worker agents produce project-correct and high-quality UI outcomes with tasteful feedback loops.
goals: Improve UI quality from worker output using an optional verifier loop
Increase contextual correctness of worker actions by catching obvious project mismatches
Keep feedback collaborative and useful rather than overly aggressive

initiatives.title: Toggleable Frontend Helper + UI Verification
initiatives.problem: Worker-created UIs can ship with functional bugs or poor visual decisions without a dedicated review pass.
initiatives.outcome: Aegis can optionally review worker-built UI with Playwriter MCP and provide corrective or taste-improvement feedback.
requirements: Add a toggleable feature flag for frontend verification (enabled or disabled per session/run)
Load frontend skill in Aegis context for UI-related tasks
Set up Playwriter MCP integration for UI validation against live rendered output
If functional or severe UX bugs are found, send explicit blocking feedback to worker with required fixes
If only quality/taste improvements are found, send non-blocking feedback with collaborative tone and concrete suggestions
Define a lightweight UI review rubric to represent good taste (layout hierarchy, spacing rhythm, typography choices, color coherence, responsive behavior, accessibility basics)
acceptance_criteria: When verifier toggle is off, Aegis does not run UI review and workflow remains unchanged
When verifier toggle is on and UI has clear bugs, Aegis requests fixes before completion
When verifier toggle is on and UI is functional but weak stylistically, Aegis sends improvement feedback without blocking
Feedback messages are specific, actionable, and framed constructively
dependencies: Playwriter MCP setup and connection availability
Frontend skill availability in Aegis execution context
non_goals: Enforcing rigid style preferences that ignore project design direction

initiatives.title: Proactive Context-Aware Worker Correction
initiatives.problem: Workers can produce outputs that ignore obvious project context (for example generating raw HTML in a Next.js codebase).
initiatives.outcome: Aegis catches context mismatches and redirects workers toward project-appropriate implementations.
requirements: Before validating worker output, inspect repository context (framework, conventions, current directory intent)
Create mismatch detection rules for common cases (Next.js, React, routing/layout conventions, component vs static file expectations)
When mismatch is detected, provide corrective feedback that references current project context and expected output format
Support proactive intervention when user intent and worker artifacts diverge in obvious ways
Keep interventions sensible and limited to high-confidence corrections
acceptance_criteria: In a Next.js project, a request like 'create a hero section' results in component-based guidance rather than acceptance of standalone HTML output
Aegis flags obvious context mismatches before task completion
Worker receives corrective instructions with file-format and location guidance
False-positive rate is low for standard framework conventions
non_goals: Blocking on ambiguous stylistic preferences when project context is unclear
Deep framework linting that duplicates existing CI/lint pipelines

phase_order: 1) Playwriter MCP setup + verifier toggle plumbing
3) Context detection and proactive mismatch guardrails
4) Tuning thresholds to reduce false positives
success_metrics: Reduced number of worker UI revisions caused by obvious bugs after verifier adoption
Higher rate of project-context-correct first-pass worker outputs
Positive user sentiment on Aegis feedback tone and usefulness

open_questions: How should good-taste guidance be encoded: fixed rubric only, prompt examples, or both?
Should verifier toggle default to on for frontend tasks or remain opt-in globally?
What confidence threshold should trigger blocking vs non-blocking feedback?
